_comment:
CAN dictionary for the FA24 Early (Ascent, Legacy / Outback XT; FA24DIT engine on the SH72544R) ROMs: deliverables/fa24/can/ (FA24_Early_CAN.json / .dbc / .md / _RAM.csv).

The Ascent's network selector picks a fifth network variant (flag 0x01, read in LT8H300D 0x21F1EC) whose ID table has
none of the FA20DIT frame IDs, so the FA20DIT dictionary does not apply. What the Ascent receives and sends comes from
its own code run in the emulator (my research notes, results in my research notes<CALID>.emu.json): every
receive bit flipped and the RAM it changes recorded, every RAM bit the transmit packer reads flipped and the frame bits
it changes recorded.

Fields: one per run of frame bits (within a byte) that lands on, or comes from, the same RAM byte.
Names: each field's RAM byte (LT8H300D) is carried to the 2021 WRX (LF9K000D) through the exact pair map read
backwards (samecode_specs.RamMap, LT8H300D from LF9K000D: a unique vote, else the shift of the nearest mapped
addresses on both sides within 64 bytes). Where the WRX dictionary (deliverables/can/dictionary.json) has a signal on
that RAM byte in the same direction and the field is a value (4 bits or more), the field takes its name and meaning
("same ECU variable as WRX 0x...", inferred: the bit layout and scale in the Ascent frame are not checked against it).
Flags keep a raw name (the dictionary gives RAM per byte, not per bit) and mention the WRX signal on that byte.
Received frames: the decoder's variant-4 path (LT8H300D 0x0AE6E2) copies each frame's first byte and the low nibble
of its second byte to RAM (FFF8AA7A.. for 0x139 / 0x13A / 0x13B, read), and takes payload bits only under conditions
on other ECU state (FFF8A987 and receive flags) that a one-frame emulation does not meet; so only those 30 fields are
mapped, and the payloads are not yet. The 2020 and
2019 builds are compared with LT8H300D field by field through their own maps.
